issues.display_title: Issue #558: Mobile OTP Extension for Emergency Magic Link API
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Mobile OTP Extension for Emergency Magic Link API

  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Target Project: panorra-api-go-new
  • Related Project Board: Panorra API Go New - Development (View 7: Development - Board)
  • Task Specification: docs/tasks/2026-10-22/mobile_magic_link_otp.md
  • Related Tasks / Issues:
    • Issue #553: Request Emergency Email Magic Link API
    • Issue #554: Verify Emergency Email Magic Link API
    • gothru-sso#22: Emergency Email Magic Link Login Fallback

1. Summary

Extended the Emergency Magic Link authentication system to support Mobile clients via 6-digit email OTP codes alongside existing PWA link verification:

  1. Request Endpoint (POST /auth/magic-link/request):

    • Added platform field to magicLinkRequestBody.
    • Integrated isMobilePlatform(platform): returns true if strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(platform)) == "mobile". Defaults to PWA when omitted or empty.
    • For mobile: generates cryptographically secure 6-digit OTP (100000 - 999999) using crypto/rand.
    • Stores OTP in Redis (magic_link:otp:<email>) with 15-minute TTL.
    • Queues email to RabbitMQ with template "email_magic_link_otp".
    • Shared rate limiting (3 requests / 15 minutes) and unregistered account handling preserved.

  2. Verify Endpoint (POST /auth/magic-link/verify):

    • Registered dedicated POST route for mobile OTP verification.
    • Request body model: type verifyMagicLinkOtpRequestBody struct { Email string; Otp int }.
    • Single-use consumption: verifies and deletes OTP from Redis (consumeMagicLinkOtp).
    • Shared login finalization (finalizeMagicLinkLogin): updates is_email_verified = true, restores user if deletion requested, refreshes Redis session, generates Hasura JWT, and returns standard login envelope with fallback: "magic_link".

  3. Email Template (email_magic_link_otp.html):

    • Created GoThru-branded responsive template with 6-digit code badge, 15-minute expiry warning, and security note.
    • Registered in src/Utils/EmailTemplate/EmailTemplate.go.

2. Files Created & Updated

Created

  • src/Utils/EmailTemplate/templates/email_magic_link_otp.html: Email template for mobile OTP.
  • docs/tasks/2026-10-22/mobile_magic_link_otp.md: Task specification.
  • docs/tasks/implementations/2026-10-22/mobile_magic_link_otp_impl.md: Implementation document.
  • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Verify Magic Link OTP.yml: Dedicated POST collection request for mobile OTP verification.

Updated

  • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink.go: Added mobile request logic, OTP Redis storage, POST verification handler, and shared finalizeMagicLinkLogin.
  • src/Controllers/V1/AuthController.go: Added VerifyMagicLinkOtp controller.
  • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes.go: Registered POST /auth/magic-link/verify with ActivityLog.Wrap.
  • src/Utils/EmailTemplate/EmailTemplate.go: Registered template and handler EmailTemplateMagicLinkOtp.
  • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink_test.go: Comprehensive unit tests for mobile flow.
  • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes_test.go: Route test for POST verification.
  • src/Utils/EmailTemplate/EmailTemplate_test.go: Template rendering unit tests.
  • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Request Magic Link.yml: Added mobile request example.
  • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Verify Magic Link.yml: Added mobile OTP verify example.

3. Example Usage & API Contracts

A. Request Magic Link / Mobile OTP (POST /auth/magic-link/request)

Headers:

Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

Example 1: Successful Mobile OTP Request

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "platform": "mobile"
  }'

Response (HTTP 200 OK):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "status": "success",
    "message": "If this email is registered, a login verification code has been sent."
  }
}

Example 2: Unregistered Email (Prompt to Register First)

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "unregistered.user@example.com",
    "platform": "mobile"
  }'

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "message": "Please Register First",
    "valid": true,
    "code": "unregistered"
  }
}

Example 3: Missing Email Field

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "platform": "mobile"
  }'

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Request",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Email is required",
      "input": "email"
    }
  }
}

Example 4: Invalid Email Format

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "not-an-email",
    "platform": "mobile"
  }'

Response (HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity):

{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unprocessable Entity",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Invalid email address format",
      "input": "email"
    }
  }
}

Example 5: Rate Limit Exceeded (> 3 requests per 15 minutes)

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "platform": "mobile"
  }'

Response (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests):

{
  "statusCode": 429,
  "data": {
    "status": "Too Many Requests",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Too many magic link requests. Please wait a few minutes before trying again."
    }
  }
}

B. Verify Mobile OTP (POST /auth/magic-link/verify)

Headers:

Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

Request Body Schema:

Field Type Required Description
email string Yes User account email address
otp integer Yes 6-digit verification code received via email (100000 - 999999)

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description
ec string No Optional response encryption flag ("true" / "false")

Example 1: Successful Mobile OTP Verification & Login

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/verify" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "otp": 123456
  }'

Response (HTTP 200 OK):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Login success",
    "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
    "fallback": "magic_link",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "username": "user_example",
    "total": 0,
    "is_back": false,
    "onboarding_completed": false,
    "is_complete": {
      "is_password": true,
      "is_email": true,
      "is_email_verified": true
    }
  }
}

Example 2: Invalid or Expired OTP

(Triggered if OTP code does not match, has expired after 15 minutes, or has already been used)

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/verify" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "otp": 999999
  }'

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Request",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Magic link OTP is invalid or has expired"
    }
  }
}

Example 3: Missing OTP Parameter

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/verify" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com"
  }'

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{

  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Request",

Example 4: Missing Email Parameter

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

Example 5: Invalid Email Format

Response (HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity):

go test -count=1 -v ./src/Action/V1/Auth ./src/Utils/EmailTemplate ./src/Routes/V1

    • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Verify Magic Link.yml
    • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Verify Magic Link OTP.yml
  • Date: 2026-10-22

1. Problem & Context

The Emergency Magic Link fallback flow previously only supported PWA (website) via clickable link URLs containing JWT tokens (GET /auth/magic-link/verify?token=...).

For Mobile clients:

  1. Deep-linking / browser URL redirects from emails into mobile apps introduce friction and platform dependency.
  2. Mobile apps require an in-app verification flow using a numeric verification code (OTP) sent to the user's email.
  3. The existing PWA flow must remain 100% backward compatible without breaking changes for web users.

2. Scope

  1. Request Endpoint (POST /auth/magic-link/request):

    • Accept JSON body with optional platform field: { "email": "user@example.com", "platform": "mobile" }.
    • If platform is omitted or not "mobile", default to "pwa" (backward compatible).
    • If platform == "mobile":
      • Generate secure 6-digit OTP code (100000 - 999999) using crypto/rand.
      • Store OTP in Redis key magic_link:otp:<email> with 15-minute TTL.
      • Dispatch email via RabbitMQ (_send_email) using template email_magic_link_otp.
      • Return HTTP 200: "If this email is registered, a login verification code has been sent.".
    • Maintain anti-enumeration protection and shared rate limiting (max 3 requests per 15 minutes per email).

  2. Verify Endpoint (POST /auth/magic-link/verify):

    • Register POST /auth/magic-link/verify dedicated to mobile OTP verification.
    • Accept JSON body: { "email": "user@example.com", "otp": 123456 } where otp is strictly integer.
    • Validate and burn OTP from Redis atomically (single-use guarantee).
    • If invalid or expired, return HTTP 400 Bad Request.
    • On success, resolve user, mark is_email_verified = true, reactivate account if requested, refresh user session in Redis, issue Hasura JWT, and return standard login response with fallback: "magic_link".

  3. Email Template (email_magic_link_otp.html):

    • Responsive GoThru-branded template featuring GoThru styling, clear 6-digit OTP display badge, 15-minute expiry warning, and security disclaimers.

  4. Testing & API Collection:

    • Add unit tests for platform detection, OTP generation, validation, Redis fallback, routing, and email rendering.
    • Update API collections with mobile request and verification examples.

3. Behavior Boundary

  • PWA Non-Breaking: GET /auth/magic-link/verify?token=... and requests without platform remain completely untouched in behavior and contract.
  • Strict Typing: otp in verification request body is strictly int.
  • Single-Use: OTP is burned upon verification to prevent replay attacks.
  • Privacy Rule: No user_id is exposed in request or cached payloads.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /auth/magic-link/request with platform: "mobile" generates 6-digit OTP and sends OTP email.
  • Requests without platform continue to send PWA magic link.
  • POST /auth/magic-link/verify accepts { "email": "...", "otp": 123456 } and returns authenticated login session.
  • Incorrect or expired OTP returns HTTP 400.
  • Reusing an OTP returns HTTP 400.
  • All unit tests pass cleanly with 100% success rate.

issues.display_title: Issue #559: Database Transaction Atomicity for User Block and Deactivation Workflows
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Database Transaction Atomicity for User Block and Deactivation Workflows

  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS

1. Summary

Enforced strict ACID transaction atomicity across user block and account deactivation workflows in panorra-api-go-new:

  1. Atomic User Block (executeBlockUserTransaction in social_helpers.go & BlockUser.go):

    • Consolidated deletion of shared bookmarks, deletion of mutual followers, and bidirectional UserBlocks creation into Config.DB.Transaction.
    • Deferred Elasticsearch counter updates until after the transaction successfully commits.

  2. Atomic Account Deactivation (DeactiveUser.go):

    • Moved active delete request check before OTP consumption to avoid burning verification codes on conflict.
    • Wrapped OTP deletion, UsersRequestDelete insertion, and user.is_active = false update in an atomic Config.DB.Transaction.
    • Invalidation of Redis deactive cache occurs post-commit.

  3. Automated Unit Testing (DeactiveUser_test.go):

    • Implemented TestDeactiveUser_UnauthorizedWhenUserDataFails and TestDeactiveUser_MissingOTP.

2. Files Updated & Created

  • Updated: src/Action/V1/Users/BlockUser.go
  • Updated: src/Action/V1/Users/DeactiveUser.go
  • Updated: src/Action/V1/Users/social_helpers.go
  • Created: src/Action/V1/Users/DeactiveUser_test.go
  • Created: docs/tasks/2026-10-22/user_block_and_deactivate_transaction_atomicity.md
  • Created: docs/tasks/implementations/2026-10-22/user_block_and_deactivate_transaction_atomicity_impl.md

3. Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./src/Action/V1/Users/...
# PASS (0 issues)

  • Unit Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Users/...
# PASS: 100% test suites pass cleanly (0 errors)

  • Build Check:

    go build ./cmd/...
# PASS (0 errors)
  • Area: Users / Data Integrity / Transactions / Social Relationships
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Users/BlockUser.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/DeactiveUser.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/DeactiveUser_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/social_helpers.go
  • Date: 2026-10-22

1. Problem & Context

Two critical mutating workflows in panorra-api-go-new operated across multiple database tables without transaction isolation:

  1. User Blocking (src/Action/V1/Users/BlockUser.go):
    • When a user enacted a block, the application deleted shared bookmarks (bookmark), deleted mutual follows (followers), and created bidirectional block records (user_blocks) via separate, uncoordinated database calls.
    • If block record insertion failed midway (e.g. database connection blip, constraint error), the user's bookmarks and followers were permanently destroyed without the block ever being created. Furthermore, Elasticsearch counters were decremented prematurely before the block succeeded.
  2. Account Deactivation (src/Action/V1/Users/DeactiveUser.go):
    • The handler deleted the OTP record (otp) before checking whether the user had already submitted an active delete request (UsersRequestDelete).
    • If the account was already deactivated or if updating user.is_active = false failed, the OTP was consumed and burned permanently, leaving the user with a broken state and wasted verification code.

2. Scope

  1. Atomic User Blocking (executeBlockUserTransaction):

    • Wrap bookmark deletion, mutual follower deletion, and bidirectional UserBlocks creation in a single Config.DB.Transaction(func(tx *gorm.DB) error { ... }).
    • Update Elasticsearch metrics (ElasticBookmark.AddCounterTotalBookmarksV1 and ElasticUsers.AddCounterFollowerFollowingPosts) strictly after the database transaction commits successfully.

  2. Atomic Account Deactivation (DeactiveUser):

    • Move the UsersRequestDelete duplication check before consuming the OTP.
    • Execute OTP deletion, UsersRequestDelete creation, and user.is_active = false update in a single atomic Config.DB.Transaction.
    • Update Redis deactivation cache only after transaction commit.

  3. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Create src/Action/V1/Users/DeactiveUser_test.go covering unauthorized access and missing OTP validation.

3. Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Route paths (/block, /deactive), request bodies, status codes, and JSON response shapes remain identical.
    • Redis cache invalidation and Elasticsearch metrics updates function identically upon successful execution.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • Multi-table mutations in BlockUser and DeactiveUser are fully atomic inside Config.DB.Transaction.
  • OTP is never deleted if deactivation pre-checks or database updates fail.
  • All unit tests pass cleanly (go test ./src/Action/V1/Users/...).
  • Project builds cleanly (go build ./cmd/...).

issues.display_title: Issue #560: Eliminate N+1 Database Queries and Enforce Transaction Atomicity in EditPostPanorama
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Eliminate N+1 Database Queries and Enforce Transaction Atomicity in EditPostPanorama

  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS

1. Summary

Optimized database query performance and enforced ACID transaction atomicity in src/Action/V1/Posts/EditPostPanorama.go:

  1. Eliminated N+1 Redundant SELECT Queries:

    • Pre-mapped multiple post IDs using sequence numbers into indexedMultiplePosts := make(map[int]string).
    • Replaced separate SELECT-then-UPDATE patterns with direct UPDATE ... WHERE pano_id = ? and UPDATE ... WHERE id = ?.
    • Slashed per-panorama database queries from 6 queries down to 3 queries (50% reduction).

  2. Atomic Database Transaction:

    • Wrapped all updates across little_planet_filter, animation_post, multiple_post, and posts in Config.DB.Transaction.
    • Prevented partial updates and desynchronized default thumbnails on error.

  3. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Implemented TestEditPostPanorama_UnauthorizedMissingLocals and TestEditPostPanorama_MissingSIDReturns400 in src/Action/V1/Posts/EditPostPanorama_test.go.

2. Files Updated & Created

  • Area: Posts / Query Performance / Data Integrity / Transactions
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/EditPostPanorama.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/EditPostPanorama_test.go
  • Date: 2026-10-22

1. Problem & Context

In src/Action/V1/Posts/EditPostPanorama.go, updating multi-panorama posts exhibited severe database query bloat and lack of transaction safety:

  1. Redundant N+1 SELECT Queries inside Loops:
    • For every panorama in multiples, the handler performed three redundant SELECT id queries prior to updating:
      1. SELECT id FROM little_planet_filter WHERE pano_id = ? followed by UPDATE little_planet_filter WHERE id = ?
      2. SELECT id FROM animation_post WHERE pano_id = ? followed by UPDATE animation_post WHERE id = ?
      3. SELECT id FROM multiple_post WHERE id = ? followed by UPDATE multiple_post WHERE id = ?
    • For a post with 10 panoramas, this issued 60 separate database queries in a single HTTP request.
  2. Missing Database Transaction (ACID Violation):
    • The loop updates on little_planet_filter, animation_post, and multiple_post, as well as the thumbnail default updates across posts and multiple_post, ran sequentially without a database transaction.
    • If an error occurred midway, the database was left in an inconsistent state (e.g., cleared default thumbnail flags without assigning a new one).

2. Scope

  1. Eliminate Redundant SELECTs:

    • Directly update little_planet_filter by pano_id = ?.
    • Directly update animation_post by pano_id = ?.
    • Directly update multiple_post by id = ?.
    • Pre-index multiple post IDs by sequence (map[int]string) before the transaction.

  2. Wrap in Atomic Config.DB.Transaction:

    • Execute all panorama filter updates and default thumbnail updates within a single Config.DB.Transaction(func(tx *gorm.DB) error { ... }).
    • If any step fails, all changes roll back cleanly.

  3. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Create src/Action/V1/Posts/EditPostPanorama_test.go covering unauthorized access and missing parameter validation.

3. Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Route /edit-panorama, form values (sid, pw, sl, ec, panorama_edit, sequence_edit, multiple, thumbnail_default), and JSON responses remain identical.
    • Encryption envelopes (ec=true) and status codes remain unchanged.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • Redundant SELECT id queries eliminated (50% query count reduction).
  • All database mutations are fully atomic inside Config.DB.Transaction.
  • All unit tests pass cleanly (go test ./src/Action/V1/Posts/...).
  • Project builds cleanly (go build ./cmd/...).

issues.display_title: Issue #561: Batch Insert Optimization & Idiomatic GORM Transaction in EditTrail and AddPostCompleteEmbed
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Batch Insert Optimization & Idiomatic GORM Transaction in EditTrail and AddPostCompleteEmbed

  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS

1. Summary

Refactored trail point persistence in EditTrail.go and AddPostCompleteEmbed.go to eliminate N-insert database loops, enforce idiomatic transaction handling, and eliminate UUID panic risks:

  1. Batch Insert Optimization:

    • Centralized trail point model conversion in BuildPostTrailPoints (src/Action/V1/Posts/post_edit_helpers.go).
    • Replaced for i, point := range parsedPoints { tx.Create(&pointData) } with a single GORM batch insert tx.Create(&points).
    • Network round trips reduced from N to 1 (up to 99% query overhead reduction).

  2. Idiomatic Transaction Safety:

    • Replaced manual tx := Config.DB.Begin() and manual tx.Rollback() with Config.DB.Transaction(func(tx *gorm.DB) error { ... }).
    • Guaranteed automatic rollback on both error returns and runtime panics.

  3. Panic Hazard Elimination:

    • Replaced repeated uuid.MustParse(postId) calls inside loops with a single uuid.Parse(postId) validation returning errors.New("invalid post ID format").

  4. Testing & Verification:

    • Added unit test TestBuildPostTrailPoints in src/Action/V1/Posts/post_edit_helpers_test.go.
    • All tests in src/Action/V1/Posts pass in 0.09s.

2. Files Modified & Created

    • src/Action/V1/Posts/post_edit_helpers_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/EditTrail.go

3. Verification

# PASS (0 warnings)

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Posts
# PASS (100% tests pass)

go build ./cmd/...
# PASS (0 errors)
  • Area: Posts / Trail / Performance / Transactions / Crash Prevention
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/post_edit_helpers.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/post_edit_helpers_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/EditTrail.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPostCompleteEmbed.go
  • Date: 2026-10-22

1. Problem & Context

When creating or updating trail posts (is_post = "trail"), posts have multiple GPS trail points (e.g. 50 to 500 points):

  1. Query Bloat (N-Insert Loop):
    • Both EditTrail.go and AddPostCompleteEmbed.go iterated through parsedPoints with a for-loop, executing tx.Create(&pointData) once per point.
    • For 150 trail points, this executed 150 separate network round-trips and INSERT statements to PostgreSQL inside an open transaction.
  2. Manual Transaction Risk:
    • Both handlers used manual tx := Config.DB.Begin() with individual tx.Rollback() calls on error paths. If a panic occurred, the transaction would not be rolled back, risking connection leaks.
  3. Panic Hazard with uuid.MustParse:
    • Both handlers invoked uuid.MustParse(postId) repeatedly inside the loop. If an invalid UUID string reached this stage, it resulted in a runtime panic.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Shared DTO Transformer:
    • Created BuildPostTrailPoints(postUUID uuid.UUID, parsedPoints []PostFunctions.ParsedTrailPoint) []Models.PostTrailPoint in post_edit_helpers.go.
  2. Batch Insertion:
    • Replaced individual tx.Create loop with single batch insert tx.Create(&points) in GORM, generating a single multi-row INSERT INTO post_trail_points (...) VALUES (...), (...).
  3. Idiomatic GORM Transaction:

1. Problem & Context

When creating or updating trail posts (is_post = "trail"), posts have multiple GPS trail points (e.g. 50 to 500 points):

  1. Query Bloat (N-Insert Loop):
    • Both EditTrail.go and AddPostCompleteEmbed.go iterated through parsedPoints with a for-loop, executing tx.Create(&pointData) once per point.
    • For 150 trail points, this executed 150 separate network round-trips and INSERT statements to PostgreSQL inside an open transaction.
  2. Manual Transaction Risk:
    • Both handlers used manual tx := Config.DB.Begin() with individual tx.Rollback() calls on error paths. If a panic occurred, the transaction would not be rolled back, risking connection leaks.
  3. Panic Hazard with uuid.MustParse:
    • Both handlers invoked uuid.MustParse(postId) repeatedly inside the loop. If an invalid UUID string reached this stage, it resulted in a runtime panic.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Shared DTO Transformer:
    • Created BuildPostTrailPoints(postUUID uuid.UUID, parsedPoints []PostFunctions.ParsedTrailPoint) []Models.PostTrailPoint in post_edit_helpers.go.
  2. Batch Insertion:
    • Replaced individual tx.Create loop with single batch insert tx.Create(&points) in GORM, generating a single multi-row INSERT INTO post_trail_points (...) VALUES (...), (...).
  3. Idiomatic GORM Transaction:
    • Replaced manual tx.Begin() / tx.Rollback() / tx.Commit() with Config.DB.Transaction(func(tx *gorm.DB) error { ... }), providing automatic rollback on errors and panics.
  4. UUID Validation:
    • Validated postUUID, err := uuid.Parse(postId) once before entering the transaction.
  5. Unit Testing:
    • Added unit test TestBuildPostTrailPoints in post_edit_helpers_test.go.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • All trail points are inserted in a single batch query.
  • Transactions are managed atomically via Config.DB.Transaction.
  • No unchecked uuid.MustParse calls.
  • 100% test pass rate in src/Action/V1/Posts.
  • Clean build and vet checks.
